correctness.rationale: For a>=2,b>=B(a)=102400(a+1)^6, the graph has balls of radii 0,1,2 only, hence the stated three explicit average branches at every vertex. The candidate active branch T(u,v)=(u,(X*1_b+v)/(a+1)) has two-class singular block [[1,0],[sqrt(ab)/(a+1),1/(a+1)]], giving top squared singular value Lambda=(tau+sqrt(tau^2-4/(a+1)^2))/2. Its strictly positive unique singular vector has uniform values x>y and is an actual M-active vector, so ||M||^2>=Lambda. For arbitrary nonnegative unit f, the proof bounds ||Mf||^2<=bX^2/(a+1)^2+20(a+1)sqrt(b), implying X^2>=a-Delta with Delta=20(a+1)^3/sqrt b<=1/16 for any maximizer. Cauchy-Schwarz bounds deviations in A and all values in D; the explicit inequalities enforce strictly radius-0 on A and radius-1 on D, hence every maximizer lies on T's simple leading singular vector, proving equality and all moduli. Expansion of the quadratic root yields the asserted -1/(ab) second-order correction at fixed a. Independently enumerated 1782 finite ball-selection matrices for selected K_(a,b), matching the candidate norms; these small cases do not prove the enormous sufficient threshold.

value.rationale: This is a sharp nonlinear strong-type ℓ² problem for a natural graph family not reducible to the already-solved stars/complete graphs. It identifies a whole infinite imbalance regime where a global maximal operator locks to a simple linear selection, with all extremizers and a quantified asymptotic correction. The threshold need not be optimal for the fact to be useful.
